Hello, and welcome to Idaho Reports. THIS WEEK, I sit down with Senate Minority Leader Melissa Wintrow, House Majority Leader Jason Monks, Senate Education Chairman Dave Lent, and Division of Financial Management administrator Lori Wolff to get a progress report on the legislative session. BUT FIRST, the Idaho Conservation League sent a letter to state lawmakers and the Idaho State Department of Agriculture in February, raising concerns with documented biosecurity lapses at several domestic elk farms across the state, flagging the potential of possible chronic wasting disease transmission between wild and domestic animals. CWD is a fatal neurological condition, like mad cow disease or scrapie, that affects the deer and elk family - known as cervids or Cervidae. I sat down last week with the ICL’s Wildlife Program Associate, Jeff Abrams, to hear his concerns about Idaho’s approach to preventing the disease from spreading. CG: Podcast Excerpt – CWD Domestic Cervids TBD I also reached out to the Idaho Department of Agriculture to get their response. In a written response to the Conservation League, Director Chanelle Tewalt said, “While extremely unfortunate, CWD exists at endemic levels in other states, and wildlife do not recognize state lines. There is a risk of CWD transmission without domestic cervidae operations having ever existed in Idaho.” You can hear my full interview with Jeff Abrams, and details from the exchange of letters, on the Idaho Reports podcast. That’s at youtube.com/idahoreports, or wherever you get your podcasts. MEANWHILE, at the statehouse this week, on Wednesday the House passed the “Pediatric Secretive Transitions Parental Rights Act,” building on a law passed in 2023 that bans surgical and hormonal gender affirming care for minors. This bill would prohibit healthcare providers and educators from facilitating a minor’s transition without informing the child’s parents or guardians. The bill passed on a mostly party line vote, which most people expected. The real surprise came after the vote, when House Minority Leader Ilana Rubel attempted to submit a minority report into the record, outlining the Democrats’ objections. CG: SOT – House(1?) Kyle Harris of Lewiston voiced his frustrations with the committee’s working group processes that prepare materials for the public budget hearings. Commented [MD1]: Is this accurate?
